request.instruction:
Report whether the required checks have current successful evidence. For each required check use its latest observed run on the final source snapshot; a later failure supersedes an earlier success. A receipt is valid only if its bound artifact hashes match the final inventory. Return strict JSON with exactly ready (boolean), needs_work (sorted check names), and evidence (mapping each currently successful required check to its exact run_id). Include no extra fields. A missing, failed or stale check belongs in needs_work, not evidence. Do not invent evidence or shorten identifiers.
Preserve the facts needed by the public rule after another memory reduction and a later source or artifact change. Prioritize exact snapshot/run identifiers, check names, chronological supersession, failures and artifact bindings. Public rules will be repeated; do not spend memory copying them. Use concise prose. Return only memory within the stated UTF-8 byte cap. At the second boundary use only admitted parent memory and new public observations.
Return an object with one string field memory. Its decoded UTF-8 bytes must be <= 1536.
The announced scope lists possible final check names. Keep only those checks, preserving their latest receipts on every available source snapshot. The final source snapshot and a subset of scope will be disclosed later.
